prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map supports a coarse room layout: the seated person stays in front of the camera, roughly 1–2 m away, while the bed behind them is about 2–3 m away and the wall, window, and shelving are farther back, approximately 3–5 m. Bright regions along the lower edge are very near the camera, likely within about 0.2–0.7 m, and partly occlude the person’s lower body; the person also occludes part of the bed. Across the five frames, the person remains near the lower-left or centre-left, with modest apparent distance changes caused by camera motion rather than a clear approach or retreat. Depth makes near-versus-far layering clearer than RGB, but boundaries around the person, bed, arms, and reflective or dark background areas are smoothed or merged, so the metre estimates are approximate.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map identifies a person in every frame and parts of the bed mainly in the first two frames, separating these overlapping regions more explicitly than RGB. The person is in front of the bed, roughly 1–2 m from the camera, while the bed extends behind and beside them at roughly 2–3 m; their mutual separation appears small because the person is seated immediately adjacent to or against it. The person shifts from the left side toward the centre across the sequence, while other room objects, the foreground occluder, and most furniture remain unlabelled; the lower body is partly outside the frame or hidden. The masks are unreliable in the first two frames, where person and bed regions overlap, fragment, or receive inconsistent labels, and the map provides little direct evidence for facing direction, gaze, arm’s reach, or exact distance.
descriptions.pose: The pose map adds body and hand geometry that is difficult to isolate in RGB: a partial yellow upper-body/arm skeleton appears in the second frame, a magenta hand appears in the second through fourth frames, and another partial yellow body appears in the fourth. These detections place the visible person about 1–2 m ahead, with arms extending laterally and hands roughly at torso or head height; the detected hands may be within that person’s arm’s reach, but no reliable camera-wearer skeleton is visible for judging the wearer’s reach. The second-frame body appears oriented partly across the image rather than squarely toward the camera, while the fourth-frame body is more upright and angled; head and face landmarks are too incomplete to determine gaze confidently. Missing detections in the first and fifth frames, floating hand detections, truncated limbs, and inconsistent skeletons make approach, retreat, occlusion, and turning estimates unreliable.
